title: Email triage: production vs. full body
summary: 36 made-up emails, each classified 2 times per variant by Claude Haiku through the dashboard's own classify.llm_verdicts. Before: the first 600 characters of each body, as the dashboard sends today. After: the first 4,000 characters.
legend: Calendar entries that shouldn't exist: 0 before, 0 after (across all repeats). Rates count only the cases where a field applies: dates caught is over emails that need a calendar entry.

triage.text: work-invite-ats-long (before): The deciding text ends at character 1113, but the classifier only sends the first 600, so the model never saw it.
work-invite-ats-relative (before): The deciding text ends at character 933, but the classifier only sends the first 600, so the model never saw it.
work-screen-ats-long (before): The deciding text ends at character 798, but the classifier only sends the first 600, so the model never saw it.

work-recruiter-cold (before): The instructions define jobStatus only for a job the person applied to and never say how to treat unsolicited recruiter outreach, so the model guessed 'acknowledged' instead of 'none'.
work-perth-time (before): The instructions say times are Australia/Sydney but never say to convert emails that state another timezone such as AWST, so the model kept 10:00 instead of 13:00.

per-delivery-slot (before): The instructions list deliveries with a fixed slot as extractable but don't say how to handle a time window (8am to 12pm) or whether it gets a start time, and the model's null time with high confidence conflicts with the gold 08:00.

work-invite-ats-relative (after): The instructions define jobStatus values but never say whether a first conversation with a hiring manager counts as interview or screening, so the model had to guess.

work-viewed (after): The instructions don't cover a job board's 'application viewed' notification, which is bulk-sent yet concerns a real application, and they don't say which jobStatus or category it gets, so the model guessed Marketing and none.
